adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the Lark refresh call was wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, whose own comment says it “should only contain the access token and expiry date” (i.e., not Lark’s normal refresh payload). The Lark code still passes that response into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which implies it expects the native Lark refresh JSON shape. Unlike other integrations updated in this diff (e.g. Google/O365/Zoom) there is no `parseRefreshTokenResponse`-style fallback here. This makes sync-mode token refresh for Lark very likely to break or produce missing fields when updating stored credentials.
